text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian federal parliament decided on Thursday to abolish the "state of imminent war danger" in the territory of the Moslem-Croat Federation. Decision on abolishing curfew will be examined by Bosnian interior ministry.
- Dutch government pledged to Bosnia $13 million for agricultural machines and other equipment.
- A private Bosnian air company "Air Commerce" will launch its first passenger flight to Maribor (Slovenia) on Friday.
- Financial police allow petrol stations to reopen in Tuzla but little or no fuel available. Paper says petrol stations have failed to pay taxes on fuel.
- The ICRC mission in Bosnia will shut down its operation on Friday in commemoration of six delegates killed in Chechnya earlier in the week. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
